key_insight: LLM routers can be trained without human labels by using synthetic queries and answers generated from high-level task descriptions, enabling accurate annotation-free skill estimation and expert selection across heterogeneous, unknown request distributions.
problem_solved: How to train routers that pick the best expert model when ground-truth labeled routing data is unavailable and user request distributions are diverse or unknown — eliminating dependence on costly human annotations.
method: Use generator LLMs and high-level task descriptions to synthesize diverse query–answer pairs that approximate real user requests.
Train a skill-estimation router on the generated dataset to predict or rank which expert/model will perform best for each input.
Deploy the router to route real queries to selected experts at inference time and evaluate robustness to distribution shifts and heterogeneous tasks.
impact: Enables practical, annotation-free multi-model routing for ML systems — lowering labeling costs and allowing dynamic, data-efficient selection of the best model per request, improving overall system accuracy and resource use.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Generator LLM → Synthetic QA dataset → Router (skill estimator) → Expert models (selected per query)
Bar chart comparing routing accuracy and model utility: RGD-trained router vs supervised baselines and random routing
Heatmap or matrix: model skill profiles across task categories (shows which expert excels where)
Icon set: reduced annotation cost, faster deployment, and robustness to unknown user distributions
paper_title: Routing with Generated Data: Annotation-Free LLM Skill Estimation and Expert Selection
paper_authors: Tianyi Niu, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Genta Indra Winata, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Supriyo Chakraborty
